design.title: Flexibility Passport — Schneider Electric Yuvva Yodha Hackathon 2026
design.style_name: Eco-Brutalist Poster (paper/charcoal monochrome + dark forest green + pastel mint/butter)

typography.heading: Anton (display) + Space Grotesk 700 (slide headings, uppercase)
typography.numeric: Anton for hero numerals, Space Mono for labels/tags

design.reference: Maxell floppy print (brutalist grey print) x retro green poster (duotone, hazard stripes, stars, barcodes) x eco brochure (pastel green blocks). Thick 3px borders, hard offset shadows, visible grids, stamps, sharp 4-point stars, arrows, hazard stripe bars, barcode strips.

slides.title: Cover — Flexibility Passport
slides.task_brief: COVER, full-bleed .slide-dark (green-deep #10352A). Mono tag row top: left 'SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC — YUVVA YODHA HACKATHON 2026', right 'FP—01 / 14', separated by 3px paper hline. Giant stacked Anton display (paper #F0EEE6): 'FLEXIBILITY' solid, 'PASSPORT' with color mint or outline effect, ~110-120px, tight leading. Subtitle (Space Grotesk 600, mint): 'Reliability-constrained energy flexibility for Indian data centres'. Three mono chips (2px paper border, transparent bg): 'PEAK-SHAVE WITHOUT FEAR' / 'DIESEL AVOIDANCE' / 'UPTIME PROTECTED'. Right side: duotone photo block — URL https://z-cdn.chatglm.cn/image-search-mcp/images-ppt/03bbdb6b6ca2.jpg in .img-tint.img-duo wrapper with 3px paper frame + hard-paper shadow, rotated ~1deg; mono caption under photo: 'FIELD 01 — INDIAN DC CAPACITY 1.5 GW → 6.5 GW'. Brutalist furniture: one horizontal .stripe-paper hazard bar, one large 4-point star (✦) in butter, one barcode strip (.barcode with paper filter/invert on dark — use white bars via inline style), rotated .stamp-paper badge 'REL-CRITICAL LAYER — v1.0'. Bottom: team placeholder block (2px paper frame, mono, paper text): 'TEAM ______________________ · MEMBERS ____ ____ ____ ____ · INSTITUTION ______________________'. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — transition into S2 = Morph; title lines: Zoom In 0.4s on click 1; photo block: Wipe from left 0.5s; chips: Appear With Previous staggered 0.1s; stamp: Fade + subtle Grow&Turn. DELIVERY — open with one line: 'We make existing buffers bankable.'

slides.title: India's Data-Centre Decade
slides.task_brief: STATS SLIDE, paper bg with faint .grid-bg. Top mono kicker tag (frame-2): '01 — PROBLEM / SCALE [R1]' left, 'FP—02 / 14' right. Heading (Space Grotesk 700 uppercase ~40px): 'INDIA'S DATA-CENTRE DECADE'. Left ~55%: three stat blocks stacked, each with Anton hero numeral + Inter label + 3px top rule: (1) '1.5 → 6.5 GW' — 'installed data-centre capacity, 2025 → 2030 projection'; (2) '0.5%' — 'of national electricity used in 2025 — both expected to more than double by 2030'; (3) '150 BN L' — 'cooling water drawn in 2025, doubling by 2030'. Supporting paragraph (Inter 500): 'Every new megawatt lands on a grid already stressing reliability, water and storage. India-specific delivery constraints flagged by policy research: electricity reliability, cooling water, BESS duty-cycle evidence and future demand-response pilots. [R1]'. Right ~45%: photo URL https://z-cdn.chatglm.cn/image-search-mcp/images-ppt/bc69a6a7c052.jpg in .img-tint.img-duo 3px frame + hard shadow; below it a mini bar infographic built from divs: two vertical bars labelled '2025 — 1.5 GW' (mint fill) and '2030 — 6.5 GW' (green fill, ~4.3x taller), framed. Furniture: one ✦ star butter, one arrow '→' accent. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — transition Morph from cover; three stats: Fade + Move Up staggered 0.15s on one click; bars: Wipe from bottom; photo: Fade. DELIVERY — let 1.5→6.5 land before speaking; then say 'and every GW expects the grid to behave'.

slides.title: Owned Assets, Unusable Flexibility
slides.task_brief: PROBLEM SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '02 — PROBLEM / THE RELIABILITY GAP'. Heading: 'OWNED ASSETS. UNUSABLE FLEXIBILITY.' Hero statement panel (.panel-mint, 3px frame, hard shadow, Inter 600 ~19px): 'A critical data centre already owns flexibility assets — but cannot confidently use them as one combined resource. It has no defensible way to translate live physical conditions into a safe, time-bound flexibility commitment.' Below it an ink strip (.panel with bg ink, paper Space Mono text): 'THIS IS A RELIABILITY PROBLEM — NOT A MONITORING PROBLEM.' Three evidence cards (3px frame, hard-sm, paper bg, Space Grotesk 700 card titles): (1) 'PEAK-SHAVING EATS THE RESERVE' — 'A battery action that pays during a peak erodes state-of-charge headroom and raises tail outage risk — the same battery cannot serve both masters. [R3][R12]'; (2) 'COUPLING IS OVER-SIMPLIFIED' — 'Demand-response models flatten the electrical, thermal and computational coupling that actually interacts inside a live facility. [R10]'; (3) 'NO WHOLE-FACILITY ENVELOPE' — 'What MW reduction, duration, ramp and recovery can one facility safely promise as a single envelope? Still an open implementation question. [R3][R9][R10]'. Footer mono strip: 'RESEARCH BASE — 15 PEER-REVIEWED PAPERS · LAB BENCHMARKS · INDIA POLICY RESEARCH [R1–R15]'. Furniture: rotated .stamp 'VALIDATED' on the statement panel corner, small ✦ stars, barcode strip bottom-right. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; statement panel Zoom In; ink strip Wipe from left; three cards Fly In from right, one per click; stamp Fade + Spin emphasis. DELIVERY — read the mint statement verbatim; it is the thesis.

slides.title: One Question No System Answers
slides.task_brief: PROBLEM-TO-SOLUTION BRIDGE, paper bg. Kicker: '03 — PROBLEM / THE HARD DECISION'. Heading: 'ONE QUESTION NO SYSTEM ANSWERS JOINTLY'. Equation banner (.panel-green, 3px frame, hard shadow): Anton paper text ~30px: 'REDUCE GRID DRAW BY X kW · FOR Y MINUTES · AT Z RAMP — WITHOUT CROSSING THE RESERVE.' with mono sub-line: '…while keeping enough thermal, electrical and operational reserve to satisfy the facility's reliability policy if a utility disturbance occurs.' Four coupling cards in a 1x4 chain with bold '→' arrows between (3px frames, hard-sm; card titles Space Grotesk 700; body Inter 500 12.5-13px): (1) 'COMPUTE → COOLING' — 'An AI training or inference surge becomes heat; cooling responds on a different timescale. A job can look safe in server-power terms and still create a thermal or hydraulic constraint.'; (2) 'COOLING → BATTERY' — 'Pre-cooling or reduced pump demand buys short-duration flexibility — then thermal recovery reshapes the battery requirement and later load.'; (3) 'BATTERY → GRID' — 'UPS/BESS can shave a peak or smooth a ramp, but every discharge reduces the buffer available if the grid fails before recharge.'; (4) 'GRID → COMPUTE' — 'A tariff peak, outage alert or utility request changes the value of flexibility — uptime still needs a believable response.' Top-right small duotone photo block: URL https://z-cdn.chatglm.cn/image-search-mcp/images-ppt/4b9d092fa3b9.jpg (.img-duo, 2px frame). Furniture: ✦ star, hazard .stripe bar thin. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; equation banner: Fade by line (title first, sub-line second); four cards: Wipe from left one per click with arrows Grow From Left With Previous. DELIVERY — this is the question the whole project exists to answer; slow down here.

slides.title: The Decision Layer (Solution Reveal)
slides.task_brief: SOLUTION REVEAL, full-bleed .slide-dark. Kicker mono mint: '04 — SOLUTION'. Giant Anton (paper): 'FLEXIBILITY PASSPORT' (~64px) + mint Space Grotesk 700 line: 'THE DECISION LAYER THAT ISSUES YOUR FACILITY'S FLEXIBILITY COMMITMENT.' Definition paragraph (Inter 500, paper, max ~52ch, 17px): 'A reliability-aware translation layer between physical infrastructure telemetry and an operational flexibility commitment. It sits ABOVE existing power, cooling and DCIM systems — consumes their trusted data, and converts it into a bounded recommendation. Later: an operator-approved command.' Flow chips row (2px paper frames, mono, paper text, connected by paper arrows): 'TELEMETRY IN' → 'SAFE-ENVELOPE COMPUTE' → 'TIME-BOUND COMMITMENT' → 'VERIFIED DELIVERY'. Bottom mono strip (mint text): 'READ-ONLY FIRST · BOUNDED COMMANDS LATER · FACILITY POLICY ALWAYS AUTHORITATIVE'. Furniture: large outlined 4-point star (✦, 3px paper border rotated square behind glyph or CSS star), .stripe-paper bar, dotgrid-paper patch, one barcode strip in paper. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph transition from light slide = the dark flip is the wow moment; title Fade + Scale 105%; flow chips Fly In from left staggered 0.12s; bottom strip Fade last. DELIVERY — pause 2 seconds after the flip; then: 'Not a dashboard. A passport.'

slides.title: The Core Output — A Safe Flexibility Envelope
slides.task_brief: SIGNATURE SLIDE — THE PASSPORT. Paper bg, faint .grid-bg. Kicker: '05 — SOLUTION / WHAT YOU GET'. Heading: 'THE CORE OUTPUT: A SAFE FLEXIBILITY ENVELOPE'. Left ~58%: passport card (3px frame, paper bg, hard shadow, mint header bar with Space Grotesk 700 'FLEXIBILITY PASSPORT — FACILITY ID FP-001'): 7 field rows, each mono label + Inter 500 value, separated by 1px hairlines: 'MAX DEMAND REDUCTION' — 'grid-demand ceiling in kW / MW'; 'MAX SUSTAINABLE DURATION' — 'minutes the envelope holds'; 'MAX RAMP RATE' — 'kW per minute'; 'RECOVERY' — 'expected recovery time + recovery load'; 'LEVERS' — 'flexible compute · cooling adjustments · charging changes · BESS/UPS discharge'; 'PROTECTED RESERVE' — 'contingency + reliability threshold that cannot be crossed'; 'CONFIDENCE' — 'validation status of this commitment'. Right ~42%: butter stamp panel (.panel-butter, 3px frame, hard shadow): Space Grotesk 700 title 'ISSUED — DEMO VALUES'; mono rows: '420 kW FOR 18 MIN' / 'RAMP ≤ 150 kW/MIN' / 'BESS RESERVE ≥ 42%' / 'RECOVERY ≤ 11 MIN'; micro mono footnote: 'ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO NUMBERS — NOT CLAIMS ABOUT A REAL SITE'; rotated .stamp 'CONDITIONAL BY DESIGN' overlapping panel corner. Furniture: barcode strip, ✦ stars, one arrow accent. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; passport card Zoom In; the 7 rows Appear staggered top-to-bottom 0.08s on one click; butter panel Fade + subtle Spin (5deg) emphasis. DELIVERY — 'Every commitment is issued like a document: bounded, signed, auditable.'

slides.title: Inside One Flexibility Event
slides.task_brief: PROCESS SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '06 — HOW IT WORKS / EVENT LOOP'. Heading: 'INSIDE ONE FLEXIBILITY EVENT'. Five numbered blocks in a horizontal strip (each 3px frame, hard-sm; giant Anton step numerals 01–05 in green; Space Grotesk 700 titles; Inter 500 12.5px bodies; bold '→' between blocks): 01 'READ' — 'Facility state: load, criticality, cooling conditions, ambient, UPS/BESS state, generator status.'; 02 'COMPUTE' — 'Largest available safe envelope under current constraints.'; 03 'DISPATCH' — 'Coordinated plan: pre-cool within thermal limits · defer non-urgent batch job · pause non-critical charging · discharge only BESS energy above protected reserve.'; 04 'REJECT' — 'Any plan breaching reserve, battery-health, temperature, water or workload-criticality constraints.'; 05 'VERIFY' — 'Delivered vs promised: kW reduction, duration, minimum SOC, cooling temperatures, recovery time.' Block 04 visually distinct: .panel-butter bg + rotated .stamp 'THE GATE' — caption under strip: 'Step 04 is why reliability stays non-negotiable.' Bottom mono strip: 'THE LOOP REPEATS — EVERY EVENT ISSUES, EXECUTES AND AUDITS A COMMITMENT.' Furniture: ✦ stars, arrows. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; blocks 01→05 Wipe from left, one per click 0.3s; arrows Grow From Left With Previous; block 04 Pulse once after appearing. DELIVERY — walk the strip left to right; land on 04: 'most software lacks this gate'.

slides.title: Architecture — Five Layers
slides.task_brief: TECH STACK SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '07 — TECH / SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE'. Heading: 'FIVE LAYERS. ZERO CHANGES TO PROTECTION LOGIC.' Left ~58%: vertical stack of 5 layer bars (top 05 → bottom 01; each 3px frame, hard-sm; mono layer number + Space Grotesk 700 layer name + Inter 500 12.5px description; alternate panel-grey / paper backgrounds; layer 03 highlighted with .panel-green): 05 'VERIFICATION' — 'Compares promised vs delivered performance; records the minimum reserve actually maintained.'; 04 'ACTION' — 'Time-bound plan + audit trail. Early pilot: read-only or bounded, operator-approved commands.'; 03 'FLEXIBILITY ENGINE' — 'Searches for the largest useful load reduction satisfying ALL hard constraints. Flexibility is CONDITIONAL — never a fixed battery-size number.'; 02 'STATE & CONSTRAINTS' — 'Telemetry → operational state. Hard limits: electrical reserve · thermal · hydraulic · battery · workload criticality · recovery.'; 01 'INPUTS' — 'Grid load · IT/rack power · workload criticality · UPS/BESS SOC · generator state · cooling load & flows · weather · water · tariff/event signals.' Right ~42%: 'THE CONTROL LOGIC' (.panel-green, 3px frame, hard shadow): Space Mono intro 'MAXIMISE usable grid reduction SUBJECT TO:'; mono list: 'minimum reliability reserve' / 'thermal + hydraulic limits' / 'battery operating limits' / 'workload criticality' / 'recovery requirements'; divider; Space Grotesk 700 punchline: 'OUTPUT ≠ "USE THE BATTERY" — OUTPUT = A PORTFOLIO across compute · cooling · storage.' Below: mono note chip: 'LAYERED SO IT CAN BE PROTOTYPED WITHOUT MODIFYING CRITICAL PROTECTION.' Furniture: ✦ star, thin .stripe bar. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; layer bars Fly In From Bottom stacked staggered 0.12s (05 first); right panel Fade after; punchline Bold Reveal / font emphasis. DELIVERY — stress 'conditional, not a fixed number' — that single line separates this from every battery scheduler.

slides.title: Above Schneider — Never Instead of It
slides.task_brief: STRATEGIC FIT SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '08 — FIT / SCHNEIDER ALIGNMENT'. Heading: 'ABOVE SCHNEIDER — NEVER INSTEAD OF IT.' Left column titled 'WHY IT PLUGS INTO ECOSTRUXURE' (Space Grotesk 700) with 3 rows (3px frames or hairline dividers, Inter 500): (1) 'EcoStruxure IT Advisor already exists as a vendor-agnostic DCIM / digital-twin platform for power, cooling, environmental and asset data. [D4]'; (2) 'The Passport consumes that telemetry and asset model — it does not recreate the monitoring stack.'; (3) 'The new problem narrows to one decision:' followed by a mint highlight quote block (Space Grotesk 700 ~20px): '"WHAT MAY THE WHOLE FACILITY SAFELY PROMISE RIGHT NOW?"'. Right column titled 'DELIBERATE GUARDRAILS' with 3 rows, each led by a bold '✕' glyph in green + Inter 500 body: (1) 'Does NOT replace EcoStruxure, a BMS or hard electrical protection — they remain the field/control layer and trusted system of record. [D4]'; (2) 'Does NOT require live utility-market integration for first proof — initial value is operational: peak management, diesel avoidance, better use of existing renewable / storage assets.'; (3) 'Does NOT autonomously override critical protection — the facility-defined reliability policy remains authoritative.' Bottom mono strip: 'AN OPTIMISATION LAYER WITH A GOVERNANCE CONTRACT — NOT AN UNCONTROLLED PROTECTION SYSTEM.' Furniture: rotated .stamp 'PILOT-SAFE', ✦ star, barcode. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; left rows Appear staggered; the quoted decision line gets a Wipe highlight bar (mint) then font scale emphasis; right guardrail rows Wipe From Right one per click; bottom strip Fade. DELIVERY — this slide answers the judges' unspoken question: 'will this fight our stack?' — answer: no, it feeds on it.

slides.title: The Two-Minute Proof
slides.task_brief: DEMO SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '09 — DEMO / 3D TWIN + LIVE SIMULATION'. Heading: 'THE TWO-MINUTE PROOF'. Mono intro line: '3D IS THE EXPLANATION LAYER — THE SIMULATION IS THE EVIDENCE.' Left panel 'THE 3D SITE SHOWS' (3px frame, hard-sm; 5 compact rows Inter 500 12.5-13px with mono bullets): 'Building + electrical path — utility, switchgear, UPS/BESS, generator' / 'IT halls grouped by criticality + approximate power draw' / 'Cooling path — chillers/CDUs, loops, temperatures, thermal headroom' / 'Operator panel — load · SOC · critical load · cooling · safe flexibility · event status' / 'Constraint indicators — protected reserve · thermal limit · battery limit · blocked actions'. Right panel 'SIX BEATS — 120 SECONDS' (3px frame, hard-sm): numbered mono beats 01–06: '01 NORMAL OPS — live load, cooling, reserve' / '02 GRID-STRESS EVENT — envelope computed' / '03 COORDINATED PLAN — every lever's contribution visible' / '04 NAIVE PEAK-SHAVING — side-by-side, overdraws BESS' / '05 INJECT OUTAGE — Passport survives; naive runs short' / '06 VERIFICATION — promised vs delivered · min SOC · recovery · diesel impact'. Beat 05 highlighted (mint bg). Bottom full-width butter statement card (.panel-butter, 3px frame, hard shadow, Space Grotesk 700 ~19px): 'SAFE FLEXIBILITY: 420 kW FOR 18 MIN · RAMP ≤ 150 kW/MIN · BESS RESERVE ≥ 42% · RECOVERY ≤ 11 MIN' + right-aligned micro mono: 'ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO VALUES'. Furniture: ✦ stars, arrow accents, thin .stripe bar. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; left rows Appear staggered 0.08s; SIX BEATS: one beat per click, Wipe From Left (this is the pacing slide for live narration); beat 05 Pulse; butter card Zoom In + Pulse once. DELIVERY — offer judges the side-by-side replay first; the outage injection at beat 05 is the memory moment.

slides.title: Impact — E · S · G
slides.task_brief: ESG SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '10 — IMPACT / ESG'. Heading: 'IMPACT WITHOUT ERODING TRUST'. Three equal columns, each: giant Anton letter ('E' mint panel / 'S' butter panel / 'G' panel-grey) + Space Grotesk 700 column title + 4 compact Inter 500 rows (12.5-13px, hairline dividers): E 'ENVIRONMENTAL': 'Peak-demand reduction cuts grid energy in high-cost, high-stress hours' / 'Diesel avoidance is the stated first use case — fewer unnecessary generator runs while reserve stays protected' / 'Water + thermal constraints live inside the envelope, not bolted on' / 'Better dispatch lifts utilisation of storage + renewables'. S 'SOCIAL / RESILIENCE': 'Reduce load without silently eroding uptime protection for critical services' / 'Transparent action log — which assets contributed, why an action was blocked' / 'Implicit risk judgement becomes an explicit, repeatable operating policy' / 'Operators gain an auditable narrative for every event'. G 'GOVERNANCE': 'Every commitment is time-bound and tied to a defined reliability threshold' / 'Records promised vs delivered, reserve margin, cooling conditions, recovery time' / 'Hard protection logic + operator-approved policy stay authoritative' / 'Optimisation layer cannot quietly become a protection system'. Bottom mono strip (frame-2): 'MECHANISMS SUPPORTED BY RESEARCH [R1–R3] [R8–R12] — QUANTIFIED ROI IS A PILOT OUTPUT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION.' Furniture: ✦ stars on column tops, thin hazard bar. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; three columns Fly In From Bottom staggered 0.15s; each column's rows Appear staggered on the same click; bottom strip Fade last. DELIVERY — one sentence per column; spend the saved time on governance — it differentiates.

slides.title: Business Viability
slides.task_brief: BUSINESS SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '11 — BUSINESS VIABILITY'. Heading: 'OPERATIONAL VALUE NOW. MARKET VALUE NEXT.' 2x2 quadrant grid (each cell 3px frame, hard-sm, giant Anton index numeral + Space Grotesk 700 title + Inter 500 body 12.5-13px): 01 'PEAK COST ↓' — 'Lower exposure to peak electricity costs where tariff structures reward lower maximum demand.'; 02 'DIESEL OPEX ↓' — 'Stored energy + flexible load instead of backup generation for non-outage events — fuel and generator operating costs fall.'; 03 'DR-READY REVENUE' — 'A credible flexibility commitment unlocks future demand-response participation — future-ready, not a first-pilot dependency.'; 04 'IDLE RESERVE, USED' — 'Part of the flexibility that over-conservatism leaves untapped becomes usable — a hypothesis the pilot validates.' Below grid, category-validation strip (3px frame, Inter 500): 'CATEGORY DE-RISKED — GOOGLE demand-flexible compute [D1] + MICROSOFT power capping across millions of servers [D2] prove the behaviour; both are proprietary hypercaler stacks. That gap is our opening.' Bottom two chips side by side: butter chip mono 'NO INVENTED PAYBACK — ROI MEASURED IN PILOT: TARIFF · DIESEL COST · LOAD PROFILE · BATTERY POLICY · BASELINE'; mint chip mono 'DEPLOYABLE — SOFTWARE LAYER · READ-ONLY PILOT VIA EXPORTS/APIS · SYNTHETIC-DATA PROOF BEFORE ANY LIVE SITE'. Furniture: ✦ star, barcode strip. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; four quadrants Fade + Move one per click (clockwise); validation strip Wipe From Left; two chips Fade together last. DELIVERY — honesty is the credibility play: name the limitation before a judge asks.

slides.title: MVP Pilot & Success Criteria
slides.task_brief: VALIDATION SLIDE, paper bg. Kicker: '12 — VALIDATION / MVP + PASS CONDITIONS'. Heading: 'JUDGE US ON SAFETY — NOT ON POLISH.' Left column 'THE MINIMUM VIABLE PILOT' (Space Grotesk 700 title; 4 rows Inter 500 with mono index M1–M4, 3px frames or hairlines): M1 'Synthetic or historical site data with explicit normal-peak events and outages injected at random times' / M2 'Baseline comparison: normal operation vs naive peak shaving' / M3 'A chosen reserve/SLA condition enforced as a HARD constraint' / M4 'Report: promised vs delivered kW · duration · minimum SOC · cooling conditions · recovery time · estimated energy/diesel impact'. Right column 'PROTOTYPE PASS CONDITIONS' — 5 rows each led by a butter ✦ star (Space Grotesk 700 condition name + Inter 500 12.5px): SAFETY 'never violates the chosen reserve/SLA in defined outage scenarios' / USEFULNESS 'achieves meaningful peak reduction in defined normal scenarios' / TRANSPARENCY 'every action shows a visible contribution + a constraint reason' / VERIFICATION 'promised vs delivered flexibility + reserve reported after every simulated event' / DEMO 'the entire concept is understood via a short 3D event replay — no live data-centre connection'. Bottom mono strip: 'PASS = SAFE CONVERSION OF A PHYSICAL FACILITY STATE INTO A CREDIBLE FLEXIBILITY COMMITMENT.' Furniture: rotated .stamp 'GO / NO-GO', arrows, thin hazard bar. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; left pilot rows Appear staggered; five pass conditions: star Zoom (slight overshoot) + row Fade, one per click; heading underline hl-mint Wipe. DELIVERY — read the five conditions as a contract; they are the demo's acceptance test.

slides.title: Closing — Use What You Already Own
slides.task_brief: CLOSING, full-bleed .slide-dark. Kicker mono mint: '13 — CLOSE' left, 'FP—14 / 14' right. Giant Anton (paper ~58-64px, two lines): 'USE THE BUFFERS YOU ALREADY OWN.' + mint second line: 'PROTECT THE PROMISE YOU ALREADY MADE.' Body paragraph (Inter 500, paper, max ~60ch, 16px): 'Data centres already contain valuable electrical, thermal and computational buffers. This is not another battery and not another dashboard — it is proof of when those buffers can be used together without crossing a reliability threshold, made visible, auditable and testable.' Rotated .stamp-paper trio or single stamp: 'VISIBLE · AUDITABLE · TESTABLE'. Team placeholder block (2px paper frame, mono): 'TEAM ______________________ · MEMBERS ______________________ · CONTACT ______________________'. Footer mono strips (mint, hairline-separated): 'RESEARCH BASE R1–R15 · DEPLOYMENT CONTEXT D1–D6 · SOURCE: INDIA DC PHYSICAL ENERGY RESEARCH BRIEF — 02 OCT 2026' + 'SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC YUVVA YODHA HACKATHON 2026'. Furniture: large outline star, .stripe-paper hazard bar, paper barcode strip, dotgrid-paper patch. Speaker notes: ANIMATION — Morph; headline lines Fade in sequence 0.2s apart; body Fade; stamp Fade + subtle Grow&Turn; end with stamp Pulse. DELIVERY — close by inviting judges to the live simulation: 'Two minutes. One outage. Watch the reserve hold.'
